# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (about $199, normally $299)**
- Runner's World named it best overall. It's a comfortable clip-on that stays put, with clear sound and little leakage. Each bud has physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Downsides: IPX4 water resistance, roughly 7 hours per charge, and it can be a bit quiet in heavy traffic.
- Runner's World says Bose is releasing a new open-ear pair within a month, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts.
- [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best for long or wet runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200)**
- WIRED's top pick, with 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. The reviewer submerged them without problems.
- They clip around the earlobe and leave the top of the ear free for glasses and hats.
- [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 ($180 list, as low as $125 at some retailers)**
- This is the choice if hearing your surroundings is the top priority. It has 12 hours of battery, IP55 water resistance, and physical buttons. WIRED rated it 8/10, and it has fuller bass than older bone-conduction models.
- Downsides: the neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats, and clarity is a bit lower than Bose.
- RTINGS found the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz is tougher and pairs with multiple devices. [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2 (about $80–$100)**
- An ear-hook design with IP55 water resistance and 10 hours per charge (42 with the case). SoundGuys picked it as its budget pick and lists it at $79.99 on Amazon.
- Dealectric lists it at $129.99, or about $104 with code AFSC20. That's more than the SoundGuys price, so compare before buying. [Dealectric buy link (affiliate; Dealectric earns a commission)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- [SoundGuys guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Cheapest way to try the style: JLab Flex Open (about $40–$50) or SoundPeats PearlClip Pro ($50)**
- Both are low-risk clip-ons. The JLab has less bass and detail, and the PearlClip Pro was WIRED's cheap pick.
- [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Also worth a look: Nothing Ear (Open)**
- SoundGuys' top overall open-ear pick and its pick for running. It has stronger bass than most open designs and an IP54 rating, at about $99 on Amazon (MSRP $149). [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Quick picks**
- **Sound quality:** Bose Ultra Open
- **Marathon training or rain:** Shokz OpenDots 2
- **Maximum awareness:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
- **Tight budget:** JLab Flex Open or Soundcore AeroFit 2

Open-ear models sound thinner than sealed earbuds and offer no noise isolation. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

The search results didn't include direct store links for most of these, so I've linked the review pages, which have current buy buttons for Amazon, Best Buy, and others. Prices change often.
